title: Hot Tub & Spa Safety
blurb: Keeping the hot tub safe: water quality, testing and recording, spa chemicals, slips and safety signage.
siteNotes: The venue's test and record sheet, how often it is tested and who does it.
The correct disinfectant and pH ranges the venue works to.
Where the safety signage is, and where spa chemicals are stored.

legalNotes: CHECK: the trainer names the disinfectant (chlorine or bromine) and pH as the two readings to test and record, with no target figures. Confirm the venue's ranges and testing frequency against HSE guidance for spa pools (HSG282) and the site's Legionella risk assessment.

cards.title: Hot Tub & Spa Safety
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- explain why hot-tub water must be controlled
- test, record and act on water quality
- handle spa chemicals and the area around the tub safely

cards.title: Warm water breeds bacteria
cards.body:
Our hot tub is a lovely feature for guests, but warm water is the perfect breeding ground for harmful bacteria, including Legionella and Pseudomonas. They can make people seriously ill if the water is not properly controlled.

Managing it safely is essential, not optional.

cards.title: Test, record, act
cards.body:
Keep the disinfectant (chlorine or bromine) and pH at the correct levels, and test and record them regularly throughout the day. A spa pool needs checking far more often than a swimming pool because it is warm and heavily used.

Follow the cleaning and maintenance schedule.

cards.title: Out of use, then report
cards.body: If the water ever goes cloudy, smells off, or the readings are wrong, take the tub out of use and report it.

items.title: Out of use
items.text: Take the tub out of use

cards.title: Hazardous: never mix
cards.body:
Spa chemicals are hazardous (COSHH). Use the right PPE, follow the instructions and store them correctly.

Never mix them: mixing spa chemicals can release dangerous gas.

cards.title: Slips and signage
cards.body:
Wet surfaces are slippery, so manage slip risks. Make sure the safety signage is clear and in place.

Respect the water chemistry and the tub is a safe pleasure for guests.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Warm water grows harmful bacteria such as Legionella and Pseudomonas.
- Test and record disinfectant and pH regularly through the day.
- Cloudy or smelly water, or wrong readings: take the tub out of use and report it.
- Spa chemicals are hazardous (COSHH); use PPE and never mix them.
- Manage slip risks and keep the safety signage clear and in place.

cards.q: Warm hot-tub water can grow harmful bacteria that make people ill.
cards.why: Warm water is the perfect breeding ground for harmful bacteria, including Legionella and Pseudomonas.

cards.q: Which two things must be tested and recorded regularly in the hot tub?
cards.why: Keep the disinfectant (chlorine or bromine) and pH at the correct levels, and test and record them regularly.

cards.q: A spa pool needs its water testing…
options: Far more often than a swimming pool
Once a month, like a swimming pool
cards.why: It needs checking far more often than a swimming pool because it is warm and heavily used.

cards.q: You should never mix spa chemicals together.
cards.why: Mixing spa chemicals can release dangerous gas.

cards.q: If the water goes cloudy or the readings are wrong, you should…
options: Take the tub out of use and report it
Add more chemical and keep it open
Tell guests to stay in less time
cards.why: Take the tub out of use and report it.

cards.q: Spa chemicals are hazardous and covered by COSHH.
cards.why: Spa chemicals are hazardous (COSHH), so use the right PPE and follow the instructions.

cards.q: Which of these should the safety signage around the tub cover?
cards.why: Signage covers water temperature, no diving, no glass, supervising children, and cautions for pregnancy or medical conditions.

cards.q: Wet surfaces around the tub are a slip risk to manage.
cards.why: Wet surfaces are slippery, so manage slip risks.
